titulo: Sensing & Control, IoT dashboard · Roger Avellana
descripcion: Case study: interface design for an IoT monitoring platform. Challenge, process, deliverables and results.
h1Destacado: you can read at a glance.
entradilla: Sensing & Control builds sensors to monitor industrial facilities. I designed the interface of its web platform so that operators could understand the status of every machine in seconds and act before an incident happened.

resumen.reto: The platform showed hundreds of readings in tables that were hard to interpret. Operators were slow to spot alarms, and every screen followed a different logic.
resumen.solucion: A layered dashboard (plant, machine and sensor) with prioritized alerts, a shared component system and a color code reserved for statuses only.
resumen.resultado: Incidents are spotted sooner, and the development team builds new screens with the same components, without redesigning every time.

proceso.titulo: From the table to the control panel.
proceso.intro: Design centered on the people who use the tool every day, with tests on the plant floor at every iteration.

pasos.texto: Plant visits and interviews with operators and maintenance technicians to understand what they look at first and which decisions they make.
Information architecture in three levels (plant, machine and sensor) and wireframes of the key screens.
Visual interface, time-series charts, alarm states and a component library in Figma.
Prototypes tested with operators, legibility tweaks for plant-floor screens and a documented handoff to the development team.

entregables.titulo: An interface built for the plant floor.
entregables.intro: From the overview to every component, everything answers one question: what does the operator need to know right now?
